sources.citation: Dixon, R. M. W. & Alexandra Y. Aikhenvald (eds.). 1999. The Amazonian Languages (Cambridge Language Surveys). Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. Chapters used: 4 Rodrigues 'Tupí', 5 Jensen 'Tupí-Guaraní', 6 Rodrigues 'Macro-Jê', 7 Barnes 'Tucano', 2 Derbyshire 'Carib', 13 Aikhenvald & Dixon 'Other small families and isolates'.
sources.note: p. 171: Jaikó disappeared completely; 'For Jaikó the only source is a small word list gathered and published by Von Martius'. Nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2023. Lexical evidence for the Macro-Jê-Tupian hypothesis. Journal of Language Relationship 21(1-2): 3-56.
D'Angelis, Wilmar da Rocha. 2020. Os Tapuias, ecos do passado em Macro-Jê. Polifonia (Cuiabá: UFMT) 27(48): 12-39. Dossiê IX Encontro Macro-Jê (Barra do Garças 2018).
sources.note: Nothing. Two occurrences of the name (saved lines 761 and 775), both in §5 'Os Gê e Crens de Martius' quoting/paraphrasing Martius; a full-text search for stress/accent acento/tônic/prosód/stress/sílaba/tom/tonal finds only 'um palpite com base em sílabas ou letras em comum (ex: Pon-cata-Gê > Poni-Crans)' about Martius's etymologising of ethnonyms. Jaikó/Jeikó spellings do not occur, so the synoptic Macro-Jê table does not list the language separately.

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. Tese de doutorado, Universidade de Brasília. xxiv+571 pp. §1.1.2 'Jaikó', p. 16; §3.2.1.12 (PMJ *k reflex in Jaikó); §3.3.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States the data are 'extremamente escassos, limitando-se a uma única lista de palavras coletada por Martius (1867, v. 1, p. 279; v. 2, p. 143)'; accepts only 13 items as genuinely Macro-Jê; reproduces Jaikó forms 'sem modificações'; treats Jaikó as a separate Macro-Jê family (Macro-Jê Oriental) on segmental grounds (reflex of PMJ *k appears as a coronal fricative).

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri; Vegini, Valdir; França, Maria Cristina Victorino de. 2015. Koropó, puri, kamakã e outras línguas do Leste Brasileiro: revisão e proposta de nova classificação. LIAMES 15(2): 223-277. doi:10.20396/liames.v15i2.8642302. Jaikó pp. 260-261.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Says 'só temos um vocabulário jaikó de 67 palavras (Martius, 1863, p. 143), que parece ser uma mistura de todas as línguas do Piauí' (Pimenteira/Karib, Masakará, Tupi, Maxakali look-alikes) and leaves Jaikó as 'Linguae Incertae Sedis'.

sources.citation: Rodrigues, Aryon Dall'Igna. 2002. Para o estudo histórico-comparativo das línguas Jê. In: Ludoviko dos Santos & Ismael Pontes (orgs.), Línguas Jê: estudos vários, 1-14. Londrina: UEL. (online text edition, Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú)
sources.note: No phonology content for Jaikó. Jaikó appears only in the survey of classifications: Ehrenreich added 'os Jaikó e os Gogué' to the Akroá branch; Schmidt put Jaikó with Akué; Loukotka gave the Jê family a 'seção Jaikó' with 'só a língua Jaikó'; Greenberg listed Jaikó among macro-Jê members; Rodrigues 1999 'considerando também as línguas já mortas, mas documentadas de alguma maneira, distinguiu mais um ramo, com uma só língua, o Jaikó' (Jê norte-oriental: +Jaikó). The words fonologia/acento occur only in the general plea for descriptive work on living Jê languages.

sources.citation: Rodrigues, Aryon Dall'Igna. 1986. Línguas brasileiras: para o conhecimento das línguas indígenas. São Paulo: Edições Loyola. 134 pp.
sources.note: 'língua já extinta dos índios Jaikó, que habitavam no Piauí até o século passado', of which 'muito pouco se pode dizer pelas poucas palavras que dela se conhecem'; nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Davis, Irvine. 1968. Some Macro-Jê relationships. International Journal of American Linguistics 34(1): 42-47.
sources.note: Only other primary-literature treatment of the Jeikó forms besides Ramirez et al. 2015 and Nikulin 2020; would let a reader confirm no prosodic remark exists anywhere. Very unlikely to contain a stress statement (lexical comparison of Martius's forms with Proto-Jê).

sources.citation: Loukotka, Cestmir. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages (ed. Johannes Wilbert). Los Angeles: Latin American Center, UCLA. 453 pp.
sources.note: 'Jaico or Zyeiko - extinct language once spoken on the Caninde, Gurgueia and Piaui Rivers, state of Piaui. [Martius 1867, vol. 1, p. 257, vol. 2, p. 143.]' Entry only; nothing prosodic.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1955. Les langues non-Tupí du Brésil du Nord-Est. Anais do XXXI Congresso Internacional de Americanistas, vol. II, 1029-1054. São Paulo: Anhembi.
sources.note: Glottolog's second reference for the languoid; classificatory survey re-listing Martius's data. No stress statement expected.

sources.citation: Mason, J. Alden. 1950. The languages of South American Indians. In: Julian H. Steward (ed.), Handbook of South American Indians, vol. 6: Physical Anthropology, Linguistics and Cultural Geography of South American Indians (Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 143), 157-317. Washington: Government Printing Office. (Ge section; 'III. Jeicó (Jaicó, Geicó)'; cited for Jaikó by Ramirez et al. 2015 p. 260 as 'Mason, 1950, p. 289'.)
sources.note: No phonology content. Classificatory only: 'Possibly affiliated: Acroa and Jeicó'; Camacan resemblance 'about equal to all the Ge Proper groups, except to Suya and Jeicó'; Puri-Coroado shows 'little [resemblance] with Jeicó'; bibliography 'Geico.— Martius, 1867, 2:143'.

sources.citation: Lowie, Robert H. 1946. The Jeico. In: Julian H. Steward (ed.), Handbook of South American Indians, vol. 1: The Marginal Tribes (Smithsonian Institution, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 143), p. 567. Washington: Government Printing Office.
sources.note: No phonology content. One-paragraph ethnographic notice; the only linguistic remark is 'He published a brief vocabulary (Martius, 1867, 1: 256, 279, 779; 2: 142).' Bibliography: Alencastre 1857; Cardim 1939; Martius 1867.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1939. Línguas indígenas do Brasil: distribuição e bibliografia. Revista do Arquivo Municipal (São Paulo) ano 5, vol. LIV: 147-174, 1 mapa.
sources.note: Nothing; a distribution-and-bibliography list that only points to Martius II: 143 for Žeikó.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1932. La familia lingüística Kamakan del Brasil (segunda parte del estudio de los Žè). Revista del Instituto de Etnología de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán II(2): 493-524.
sources.note: Nothing for Žeikó. 'Entre estos idiomas-že, el de los Žeikó, hoy desaparecido, ha tenido una situación independiente e importante, y es de sentir que no hayamos conservado de esta lengua más que un solo vocabulario muy corto.' The only accent remark in the paper is an orthographic convention for the Kamakan vocabularies.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens. II. Zur Sprachenkunde (Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen / Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium). Leipzig: Friedrich Fleischer. Geicó wordlist p. 143.
sources.note: Nothing. The only primary data on the language: a 67-item Latin-Geicó wordlist on p. 143 with one footnote ('Vergl. I. 279. Die eingeschlossenen Buchstaben werden stumm mitgehört'). About 28 of the 67 forms carry an unexplained acute accent, mostly on the last vowel (uschiegkó, iquaté, ijahú, grangblá, maecó, aepurgó, ayanté, y(l)rouró, scharrepiú, scharrété, oopáung, namblú, aenettá, ná, já, ae(e)rú, juckqué, mandaltú, chügkrá, nempiaepiú, cärá, u(l)epú, aenaenongsiaé); Martius's only general remark on the acute (vol. 2 p. 29, in the introduction to the Tupi dictionary, not to this list) say…

sources.citation: Wiktionary (English). Appendix: Jeikó word list — the 67-item Latin/English/Geicó table transcribed from von Martius 1867, vol. II, p. 143.
sources.note: Wordlist-only data: reproduces Martius's forms including the unexplained acute accents (mostly on final vowels) with the note that the 67-word list is 'the only extant documentation'; no statement about stress or tone.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page geic1236 (Jeicó) and reference pages 33097, 79048, 581294; English and Portuguese Wikipedia articles 'Jaikó language' / 'Língua jaicó'.
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog lists only Martius 1867 (wordlist), Loukotka 1955 and Nikulin 2020; Wikipedia articles give no phonology and cite Martius 1867, Davis 1968, Ramirez et al. 2015, Nikulin 2020.
